I'm getting used to the new update. I switched from MyFitnessPal to FatSecret, and overall, I prefer FatSecret in many ways. But, what happened with this latest update?! Everything feels less user-friendly, and some of the features that made logging food quick and easy seem to have disappeared.  What happened to “Recently Eaten” and “Most Eaten”?! Those features were incredibly convenient. Now I have to manually search or scan everything, which is a pain in the butt and makes tracking food longer and more complicated than it should. Please bring these features back!  Another major issue is inaccurate food information. I frequently scan a barcode only to have a completely different product come up, or the nutritional information is incorrect. I really wish there were a button on each food listing that allowed users to report incorrect information and submit corrections. MyFitnessPal does a better job of allowing users to flag and correct inaccurate entries. FatSecret needs something similar.   One more feature I would love to see is the ability to copy an entire meal from the previous day. I’m a creature of habit and eat many of the same meals regularly, so being able to copy yesterday’s breakfast, lunch, or dinner would be a huge time saver!  Please listen to your users! Bring back the convenient food-logging features, improve barcode accuracy, allow users to report and correct inaccurate entries, and add the ability to copy meals from previous days. These improvements would make FatSecret so much more user-friendly and would make me love the app even more!

Used to be a great app, now too many bugs and usability issues. Lifesum used to be a very good app with many useful free features. Over time, more and more basic features have moved behind the paywall. I don’t necessarily have a problem with paying — I’m willing to pay for a good product — but the current app has too many bugs and basic usability problems to justify it.  First, the meal UI has become unnecessarily inconvenient. Every time I open Lunch or Dinner, it only shows two items, and I always have to tap “More” to see the third item and beyond. This makes no sense on an iPhone, where scrolling is the natural interaction. Requiring an extra tap every single time for something this basic creates unnecessary friction. This did not used to be a problem.  Second, adding food items has become very unreliable. I often select one item, but Lifesum adds the wrong item instead. I then have to delete it and add it again, and sometimes it is still wrong. On some occasions, I have had to force-close the app and restart it, only to find that the same food item has been added multiple times.  Third, the Apple Health integration has serious synchronization bugs. Lifesum sometimes imports the same walking step data multiple times, with each duplicate showing zero calories. More seriously, it can also import the same workout multiple times. If the same workout is imported three times, Lifesum may count the calories burned three times as well, which makes the daily calorie balance completely inaccurate. I sometimes have to force-close and restart the app several times before the activity data becomes correct.  These are very basic reliability issues and should be fixed quickly. Activity and calorie tracking are core functions of an app like this. Users should not have to constantly verify whether meals or workouts were duplicated, deleted incorrectly, or counted multiple times.  My suggestions are simple:  1. Fix the reliability bugs first, especially food logging and Apple Health synchronization. 2. Prevent duplicate workouts and duplicate activity data from being counted multiple times. 3. Improve the basic usability and remove unnecessary extra taps. 4. Thoroughly test the core logging experience before putting more basic features behind a paywall.  I don’t mind paying for an app that works well. But if basic functions are unreliable and the everyday user experience keeps getting worse, users will have little reason to pay for it.  I hope Lifesum focuses not only on monetization, but also on product quality, reliability, and usability again.

Makes tracking fun!. I’ve tried several calorie and nutrition tracking apps, including some that are arguably more minimal or streamlined, but YAZIO is the one I actually enjoy using consistently. The interface is easy to understand, the food tracking works well, and I really appreciate that features like activity calories and water tracking can be adjusted or turned off depending on how you prefer to track.  What really sets YAZIO apart for me is the sense of fun. The mascot, animations, streaks, diamonds, chests, and rewards make logging food feel much less tedious and give me a reason to keep coming back to the app. It feels encouraging without making nutrition tracking feel clinical or boring.  I also like the food database, the overall design, and the flexibility of the Pro version. I know some people prefer a completely stripped-down tracker, but for me the gamification is exactly why this app works better than others I’ve tried. It turns consistency into something I actually look forward to.  If you’re someone who wants a nutrition app that is both useful and genuinely enjoyable to use, YAZIO is absolutely worth trying.

Great core app, but too many pop-ups and limited AI. I generally like YAZIO, but the constant pop-ups and repetitive coaching messages are becoming really annoying. I don’t need to be told for the 25th day in a row that adding protein powder to my breakfast is a good source of protein. I understood it the first few times.  For a while I managed to get these messages to stop, but now they suddenly seem to be back. The app too often interrupts what should be a simple process of logging food with tips, prompts, and pop-ups that I’ve already seen many times.  I’d also really like better AI integration. Not having a direct integration with tools like ChatGPT or Claude is frustrating, because YAZIO’s built-in AI doesn’t seem to have enough tools to reliably break a meal down into its individual components and let me correct them precisely. In practice, it often feels less like a true nutrition assistant and more like a slicker version of Quick Add.  I’d love an option to permanently disable nutrition tips, coaching pop-ups, and other nonessential interruptions, plus a more flexible AI workflow that makes it easy to review and edit individual ingredients. YAZIO is useful, but these issues make the experience feel much more cluttered and limited than it needs to be.  One more frustration: my partner and I both use YAZIO, and we often eat the same meal or nearly the same meal, but there’s no simple way to share a logged meal or its macros between accounts. We end up entering essentially the same food twice. Being able to send or share a meal with another YAZIO user would save a lot of time and would be especially useful for couples or families tracking together.

Unfortunately, I Lost One of My Favorite Apps. I’m writing this review mainly because I’m trying to get the attention of the YAZIO team and support.  I’ve been using YAZIO for many years. I always loved this app, considered it one of the most convenient calorie trackers available, trusted it, and recommended it to other people.  But I honestly don’t understand what has been happening to YAZIO over the past month.  First, Quick Add stops working properly. This was one of the most useful features — I could simply enter a description, calories, and nutrients manually when I already knew the exact values. Now it either doesn’t work or tries to replace manual input with AI-generated estimates that I don’t need and that are often inaccurate.  Then products that I used to scan successfully suddenly stop being recognized by the barcode scanner. On top of that, the app keeps showing tips, suggestions, and other pop-ups that I never asked for, and sometimes there seems to be no normal way to dismiss them.  People rarely take the time to leave positive reviews unless they genuinely love a product. I had wanted to leave YAZIO a great review for a long time because I genuinely liked and trusted this app. Unfortunately, I’m leaving one star now because I don’t know how else to get the developers’ attention.  Years of positive experience have been ruined for me in a matter of weeks. Something as simple as logging my food has become frustrating, and I now have to find workarounds just to enter calories and nutrients that I already know.  Please, YAZIO team, fix the basic functionality that made this app so good in the first place. I don’t need AI to guess the calories of something when I already know the exact numbers. I need Quick Add to let me QUICKLY ADD them. I need the barcode scanner to recognize products it recognized before. And I don’t want constant tips and suggestions getting in the way of simply tracking my food.  I’m not leaving one star because I hate YAZIO. Quite the opposite — I’m leaving this review because I’ve used and trusted this app for years, and I really want it to work properly again.

Разочарование в платной версии. К сожалению, опыт использования платной подписки YAZIO оказался очень разочаровывающим.  Во-первых, в платной версии невозможно полностью отключить некоторые советы и функции, которые мне не нужны. Если я оплачиваю подписку, я ожидаю иметь возможность самостоятельно настраивать приложение.  Поддержка сообщила, что достаточно пропустить советы три раза, после чего они исчезнут на две недели. На практике это оказалось не так. Мне пришлось пропускать советы на завтрак, обед и ужин в течение трёх полных дней подряд, и только на четвёртый день появилась возможность временно отключить их. Информация от поддержки оказалась неточной.  Кроме того, в какой-то момент приложение перестало распознавать мою активную подписку и начало показывать рекламу и предложения оформить Pro после практически каждого действия, хотя подписка была оплачена и действовала. Для платного приложения это недопустимо.  Также мне не нравится система учёта активности. Приложение автоматически возвращает сожжённые калории после тренировок и другой активности, из-за чего фактический дефицит значительно уменьшается. Такой подход подойдёт не всем пользователям, а гибко настроить его под свои потребности оказалось сложно.  Я обращалась в поддержку и пыталась решить эти проблемы, однако удовлетворительного решения не получила. От платного приложения ожидаешь стабильной работы, понятных настроек и возможности самостоятельно управлять функциями, за которые ты платишь деньги.
